task.title: Inspect validated extension catalogs through the developer CLI
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/645 by exposing deterministic read-only extension discovery without crossing activation or permission boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: Delegate one caller-selected root to ExtensionRegistry::discover instead of duplicating parsing or traversal.
Print deterministic records for exact authored IDs, validated kinds, entrypoints, and root-relative manifests plus an aggregate count.
Make empty roots succeed and invalid roots fail without exposing a valid prefix or partial success output.
Keep inspection read-only and document that it does not select, activate, compile, authorize, execute, mutate, or persist capabilities.

attempts.summary: Established RED CLI integration coverage for mixed, empty, and invalid extension roots.
attempts.diagnostic: The focused integration test failed because extension was not a recognized vela-dev subcommand.
attempts.patch: Added command-level expectations for deterministic mixed-kind output, a zero-count empty root, and all-or-nothing invalid-root failure.

attempts.summary: Composed immutable discovery into a minimal inspection command.
attempts.diagnostic: The extension crate already owned descriptor-anchored validation and deterministic manifest-path order, so the CLI needed only presentation and exit behavior.
attempts.patch: Added extension inspect dispatch, catalog rendering, fixtures, integration coverage, usage documentation, and milestone evidence.

attempts.summary: Hardened terminal framing after independent pre-commit review.
attempts.diagnostic: Raw authored IDs, entrypoints, paths, and diagnostics could contain tabs, newlines, or terminal control bytes and break the promised one-record and one-diagnostic framing.
attempts.patch: Applied quoted debug escaping to every untrusted field and root-scoped diagnostic, then added adversarial regression coverage before the pull request was opened.

outcome.summary: Contributors can inspect one validated extension catalog deterministically while untrusted metadata remains framed and every activation, execution, permission, and persistence boundary stays closed.

verification.command: GitHub Rust quality gate https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/actions/runs/30238846065 and substantive exact-head CodeRabbit review at https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/pull/646

lessons: A user-facing boundary should compose the security-sensitive library contract rather than grow a second parser or filesystem traversal.
Read-only metadata inspection still needs explicit negative authority boundaries because discovery is neither enablement nor permission.
Deterministic ordering is insufficient when untrusted fields can inject delimiters or terminal controls into the presentation format.
Adversarial output framing belongs in integration tests before a developer command is treated as safely inspectable.
